previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder, COPD, tobacco use, and chronic pain from prior injuries, was admitted for shortness of breath, cough, and chest pressure. He was hypoxic on arrival with an oxygen saturation of 88% on room air, improved with supplemental oxygen. Laboratory tests showed leukocytosis and hypernatremia, and a chest X-ray revealed bibasilar opacities suggestive of atelectasis, with early pneumonia not ruled out. He was treated with levofloxacin for presumed bacterial pneumonia, a dose of prednisone for COPD exacerbation, and bronchodilators. Alcohol withdrawal was managed with scheduled diazepam per CIWA protocol, and hypernatremia resolved with IV fluids. He reported chronic pain from past trauma and prior methadone use. Despite clinical improvement, he left the hospital against medical advice on hospital day three, declining discharge prescriptions but expressing intent to follow up for methadone reinitiation and housing support.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, continuous
